South Carolina-specific mechanics that ARE confirmed directly from the text: a failed knowledge test cannot be retaken the same day (next business day only); CDL Knowledge Test fee is $2.00 per attempt; CDL Application fee is $15.00; three knowledge-test attempts are covered by the original application fee; the CDL skills test has three parts taken in strict order (vehicle inspection, basic control skills, road test) and failing one section stops the test; skills-test retest fee is $25.00; return-time-if-failed schedule is 2 business days (1st fail), 7 calendar days (2nd fail), 30 calendar days (3rd+ fail); CDL skills test scores may be "banked" (credit for passed segments) under specified conditions; a CLP must be held at least 14 days before the skills test and the remainder of the skills test must be completed within 1 year of CLP issuance; CDL license expires every 8 years, or 5 years from the date the security threat assessment was passed for HAZMAT-endorsed licenses; renewal after a 9-month-or-longer lapse requires repeating the full initial-CDL process (written test and full skills test); an out-of-state CDL transfer must be completed within 30 days of establishing SC residency; a CLP may only carry S (School Bus), P (Passenger), or N (Tanker) endorsements, never HAZMAT; HAZMAT endorsement (X or H) requires TSA fingerprint-based background check/threat assessment before issuance, per 49 CFR 383.25(a)(5)(iv) which also prohibits a HAZMAT endorsement on a CLP. South Carolina's manual does not use a separate charter-bus 'C' endorsement letter (endorsement codes referenced: H, N, P, T, X, S, consistent with several other CDL-track states in this project). Content-depth rationale: South Carolina uses the same AAMVA-authored "2005 CDL Testing System" base manual as several other CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Rhode Island), organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction (combined with South Carolina's own front-matter licensing procedures into the licensing bucket: ELDT requirements, application/fees, knowledge/skills test overview, CLP rules, restriction codes, out-of-state transfer, railroad crossing violations, HAZMAT threat assessment), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section by far, split into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.8 the Hazardous Materials Glossary), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection Test (the largest single AAMVA section in this manual by raw line count), and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test combined with Section 13 On-Road Driving into one bucket. Sections naturally short in this manual (Cargo: 20 questions, Tank Vehicles: 18, Doubles/Triples: 25, Passenger: 28) were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Driving Safely (145 questions across two buckets), Hazardous Materials (105 across two buckets), Vehicle Inspection (65), School Bus (55), Combination Vehicles (60), and Air Brakes (55) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly, reflecting genuine manual depth rather than an artificial per-bucket target -- consistent with the 650-960-question range this project's other recently built CDL-track states (Kentucky 651, Louisiana 685, Oregon 702, New Mexico 725, Rhode Island 705, Montana 958) have settled on for manuals of comparable AAMVA-base length (South Carolina's extracted text, 10,022 lines, falls within that same size band).
